title: Temperature-induced effective topology in many-body ultracold atomic quantum systems
summary: Ultracold atomic quantum systems offer an unprecedentedly powerful platform for exploring interacting symmetry-protected topological phases. Here, we show that their characteristic control over temperature provides a resource for engineering effective topological regimes with no zero-temperature counterpart. Employing finite-temperature matrix-product-state calculations, we investigate experimentally accessible Hamiltonians - the interacting bosonic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger and spin-1 XXZ chains - that host a topological phase at zero temperature, as well as a fermionic dipolar ladder model…
